findings.title: Public equality operations bypass the promised ordinary stack clearing
findings.expected: The documented ordinary protect-feature guarantee covers operations that inspect payload bytes, including public trait calls unless expressly scoped out.
findings.observed: Standalone Buffer::eq and Changes::eq read the operands directly, and derived Block::eq compares Intact byte slices. Plan and Rebuilt inherit the underlying equality. The call paths invoke no cleared wrapper. Equality invoked after a strict method returns runs where the caller invokes it.
findings.impact: The caller can compare secret-bearing values without the advertised cleanup. Source confirms that the cleanup routine is bypassed. Compiler spills, readable residue and recovery of actual secrets were not established.
findings.recommendedFix: Cover library-owned payload comparisons with the ordinary policy, and document the scope of caller-side comparisons and the result types returned from strict calls.
findings.requiredVerification: Review explicit and derived PartialEq/Eq implementations and the strict result types, and check representative ordinary call boundaries in optimized supported builds.
findings.evidence: Current-snapshot source comparison at src/buffer.rs:136–145, src/correct/changes.rs:208–223, src/file/reading.rs:44–54, src/correct/plan.rs:62–77, src/file/set.rs:74–86, src/strict/files.rs:193–196, docs/API.md:29.
findings.reproduction: Static contract inspection of the listed paths. Standalone Buffer::eq and Changes::eq read the operands directly, and derived Block::eq compares Intact byte slices. Plan and Rebuilt inherit the underlying equality. The call paths invoke no cleared wrapper. Equality invoked after a strict method returns runs where the caller invokes it.

findings.title: Stack clearing documentation overstates the fixed window and panic guarantee
findings.expected: Consumer guidance describes the exact native best-effort window, the execution depth and unwind prerequisites, and the wasm and strict differences.
findings.observed: The published SPC function overwrites a fixed region below its frame and does not measure work or callback depth. The outer TLS flag defers nested wrapper calls to the outer cleanup. Aborting panics do not return to cleanup. The changelog and technical guide give an unqualified panic promise, and the API introduction omits the target exception.
findings.impact: Applications can plan secret handling against a stronger guarantee than either implementation establishes. Caller frames/buffers, closure captures and returns, registers, heap copies and other threads remain distinct.
findings.recommendedFix: Align the in-crate comments, feature text and user guides with the upstream contract and distinguish ordinary cleanup from process isolation and the protected strict stack.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-check the same text against the exact SPC release source and documentation for native unwind, native abort, nested callbacks, strict, and WebAssembly.
findings.evidence: Current-snapshot source comparison at Cargo.toml:23–28, README.md:70, SECURITY.md:16–19, CHANGELOG.md:6, docs/API.md:29, docs/TECHNICAL.md:154, src/stack.rs:13–28, src/correct/changes.rs:63–71, SPC 0.2.0 src/stack.rs:80–106.
findings.reproduction: Static contract inspection of the listed paths. The published SPC function overwrites a fixed region below its frame and does not measure work or callback depth. The outer TLS flag defers nested wrapper calls to the outer cleanup. Aborting panics do not return to cleanup. The changelog and technical guide give an unqualified panic promise, and the API introduction omits the target exception.

findings.title: CI does not execute the supported browser target
findings.expected: RUST-16 requires a runner for supported targets with a feasible runtime and a recorded exception for targets that need one.
findings.observed: The pinned wasm32-unknown-unknown target is only linted in CI. Native jobs cover x86-64/AArch64 Linux and one hosted macOS and Windows variant. There is no Android or iOS runtime job or formal target runner inventory.
findings.impact: The release can be packaged without its CI exercising wasm fallback, and target-dependent protection claims are supported by fewer executions than the documentation suggests.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a nonempty wasm32 runtime job and record exact native/mobile runner coverage in TARGETS.md, including permitted unavailable runners. Keep bare-metal lint coverage identified.
findings.requiredVerification: Confirm a CI run on an immutable candidate executes checked public answers and the platform-specific refusal paths on the designated runners.
findings.evidence: Current-snapshot source comparison at rust-toolchain.toml:6, README.md:68–70, SECURITY.md:13–16, .github/workflows/ci.yml:31–43, .github/workflows/ci.yml:64–80.
findings.reproduction: Static contract inspection of the listed paths. The pinned wasm32-unknown-unknown target is only linted in CI. Native jobs cover x86-64/AArch64 Linux and one hosted macOS and Windows variant. There is no Android or iOS runtime job or formal target runner inventory.

findings.title: The release gate does not run the repository fuzz targets
findings.expected: RUST-18 calls for actual fuzz execution for a recorded budget in the release workflow.
findings.observed: The five targets are compiled and linted by CI. The packaging job depends on CI and arithmetic timing. The fuzz campaign appears only in local instructions, with no artifact or prerequisite consumed by the workflow.
findings.impact: Current automation can package a tag without the required fuzz execution evidence. This is a release assurance gap and does not demonstrate a parser or decoder error.
findings.recommendedFix: Wire the documented campaign and its logs into the release flow with explicit runtime budgets.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect the workflow graph and a candidate run showing all five target results and nonzero failure propagation.
findings.evidence: Current-snapshot source comparison at .github/workflows/ci.yml:45–48, .github/workflows/release.yml:14–35, fuzz/Cargo.toml:14–45, AGENTS.md:24–30.

findings.title: Second cyclic correction pass still allocates erasure metadata
findings.expected: The implementation comment describes exactly which allocations the second pass reuses.
findings.observed: Both passes reuse the syndrome and search buffers. each_word recomputes sorted_places for each pass and can allocate flags and sorted indexes again. The second failure occurs before output mutation.
findings.impact: The comment incorrectly suggests the second pass can run entirely in first-pass memory. The documented correction atomicity is maintained.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify the internal comment or share the erasure metadata as a separate change if allocation reuse is intended.
findings.requiredVerification: Check both pass entry points and the failure-before-write boundary.

findings.title: Android Clippy rejects both const thread-local initializers
findings.expected: The pinned toolchain passes the repository lint configuration on supported targets.
findings.observed: On aarch64-linux-android, Clippy reports missing_const_for_thread_local at both macro sites even though both initializers already use const blocks. The crate denies clippy::all, so the target lint exits 101. The locked cargo check for the same target succeeds.
findings.impact: The current Android protection claims lack a clean target lint result. The diagnostics do not establish a runtime TLS or wipe defect.
findings.recommendedFix: Isolate the pinned Clippy target behavior, then use a documented narrowly scoped toolchain fix or exception when available.
findings.requiredVerification: Re-run the normal locked Android Clippy command and obtain real device or emulator checks for the ordinary and strict paths.

grants.grant: Read/write guarded pages, locking, child and dump flags
grants.purpose: Keep owned payload and scratch in protected allocations
grants.admits: Ordinary work can run after a denied flag; native mappings can exhaust a process limit. Windows WER registration and working set limits affect the process.
grants.narrowestForm: Check actual properties for strict calls and lock only allocations that need it.
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for the documented behavior within the stated scope.
grants.order: Allocate zeroed area; set protections; strict admits or drops; fill; erase on writable drop before releasing mappings.

grants.grant: Dedicated pthread with bounded protected stack
grants.purpose: Run strict arithmetic and callbacks while stack has required OS properties
grants.admits: Uses the process/thread/lock budget. Unwind payload or callback output can leave the worker by contract.
grants.narrowestForm: Run one joined local operation on the small protected mapping. Fail if flags or stack unavailable.
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for the documented behavior within the stated scope.
grants.order: Verify protections before creating thread; run and join; wipe pages; deliver result or rethrow.

grants.grant: Fork generation tracking and sealed Held/HeldMut
grants.purpose: Admit known allocations and reject stale owners in a child
grants.admits: Borrowed slices taken before fork are not revalidated; supported applications must honor the no-fork rule and reopen child views.
grants.narrowestForm: Grant reference access to checked sealed types only; use fork-generation checks and report caller constraints.
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for the documented behavior within the stated scope.
grants.order: Protected mapping and generation metadata exist first; flags checked before borrowing in strict scope.

grants.grant: Write 128 KiB of dead stack, track outermost ordinary calls in TLS
grants.admits: Nested callbacks share a fixed window. Aborts and work outside that window can retain state. Trait comparisons bypass it.
grants.narrowestForm: Keep ordinary best effort explicit and route data-reading library operations through it.
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for the documented behavior within the stated scope.
grants.order: Mark thread; run outer and nested work; reset scope on exit; clear; return or resume unwind.

grants.admits: No native page/guard/lock/dump/fork protection for nonempty allocations. Strict data work must refuse.
grants.narrowestForm: Keep native-only protection promises separate and expose fallback flags.
grants.whyNoNarrower: Needed for the documented behavior within the stated scope.
grants.order: Reserve/zero; read or write; wipe on normal drop.

wipeLedger.behavior: Normal drop of a writable owner zeroes the whole exposed allocation before unmap/free. The native rounding tail starts zero and is outside the safe mutable view. Replaced plan buffers are dropped independently.
wipeLedger.evidence: Linux release disassembly and exact source. WASM shares the WorkArea drop contract with a boxed allocation.

wipeLedger.behavior: The Vec reserves before payload writes, then on drop zeroes used elements and its spare capacity. Numbers and protected plan storage have the same owner lifetime.
wipeLedger.evidence: Locked zeroize source. Free-time memory contents were not inspected.

wipeLedger.behavior: Exactly 128 KiB below the scrub frame after work or normal Rust unwind. One invocation of the scrub for the outer wrapped call. Bounds depend on available stack and assumed coverage depth.
wipeLedger.evidence: Fresh Linux optimized write length and synthetic marker checks in both profiles.

wipeLedger.implementation: 512 KiB selected in strict::run and SPC pthread stack
wipeLedger.behavior: Fail closed before execution when flags cannot be acquired. Join, then wipe the full accessible mapped stack, including unused slots, before releasing mapping and returning or transporting an unwind.
wipeLedger.evidence: Exact source, Linux tests and optimized wipe-length argument. Device-specific guarantees are matrix entries.

wipeLedger.behavior: Core state, block count, buffered bytes and cursor are zeroized on normal drop. Plan digest is wrapped in Zeroizing before its protected storage. The compressor, moves and finalization can create plain temporaries. File-visible digests are format metadata.
wipeLedger.evidence: Exact registry sources. No statement that every hash temporary is erased in alloc-only or WebAssembly.

wipeLedger.behavior: Explicit local zeroization for lane arrays, named no-alloc scratch and cyclic decode room. Caller-managed input/results and agrees_in comparison room belong to the caller. Late Result errors in documented file into calls produce zeroed output; early refusals preserve it.
wipeLedger.evidence: Current sources and file/refusal suites. Unwinding caller code is a separate lifetime.

wipeLedger.implementation: Buffer, Changes and Block equality; Changes::values
wipeLedger.behavior: Standalone equality does not reach scrub; nested wrapped calls inside an ordinary callback are covered only by the outer fixed window. Strict caller closures may export values.
wipeLedger.evidence: SEC001 and DOC001. No live secret, residue recovery or memory disclosure assertion.

wipeLedger.behavior: panic=abort, termination and deliberately leaked owners may bypass destructors. Wasm ordinary stack clearing is a no-op. No-alloc and alloc-only have no generic stack scrub. Strict payload calls refuse unsupported targets.
wipeLedger.evidence: Source/cfg map, Linux and wasm runtime evidence within recorded scope.
